idiom_name: ActiveRecord serialize :attr, coder: JSON (custom coder objects allowed)
implementation_notes: Rails turns the codec into a declaration: serialize :details, coder: JSON stores the attribute in one text column and loads it back deserialized, with optional type: to reject unexpected payload shapes and comparable: when a deep == should drive change detection. On PostgreSQL the adapter already converts json/jsonb columns to Hash/Array, so serialize is unnecessary there; use it on text columns, or attach a custom coder exposing dump/load to map a domain object deliberately instead of accepting any marshalable Ruby state.
code_sketch:
class Order < ApplicationRecord
  serialize :details, coder: JSON, type: Hash     # TEXT column
end

order = Order.create!(details: { "lines" => [...], "shipping" => { "city" => "Leeds" } })
order.details["shipping"]["city"]                 # => "Leeds"
pitfalls: YAML and Marshal coders can instantiate arbitrary Ruby objects from stored text; the Rails docs recommend primitives plus permitted_classes instead.
Ruby types the JSON coder does not support are silently cast (a class object becomes a String), so round-trip tests matter.
Renaming an attribute of a serialized domain class breaks previously stored rows; keep the payload primitive and evolve it with its own loader.
